lead.headline: Big Investors and Musk Lobby for Huang's Return as Nvidia Heads Into a Results Week Without Him
lead.deck: Altimeter and Atreides asked Nvidia's board to keep the door open for its ousted founder, a petition passed 160,000 signatures, and the chipmaker reports on Tuesday after its worst week on record by value lost.
body: The fight over who should run the world's most important AI chipmaker spilled into the open over the weekend. Brad Gerstner of Altimeter Capital and Gavin Baker of Atreides Management published an open letter asking Nvidia's board to run a careful succession process that leaves room for Jensen Huang to come back, while stopping short of demanding his immediate reinstatement. A 'Stand with Jensen' petition has gathered more than 160,000 signatures, and Elon Musk said on X that he was signing it.

Huang resigned as chief executive and director on 12 November amid reports about his personal conduct and an independent board investigation. The board has installed finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO, says it will weigh internal and external candidates, and has said it has not formally engaged anyone, despite a Financial Times report that it approached Arm's Rene Haas. The FT also reported that Huang has discussed a possible return with confidants; analysts are divided on whether that is realistic.

The market damage has been severe. Nvidia lost roughly $650 billion of value last week, its largest weekly loss on record, sliding about 13% and dropping below a $4 trillion market capitalisation. HSBC cut the stock to hold and slashed its price target to $170 from $365. Despite that, the S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq each gained more than 2% on the week, their best showing since August, and US index futures edged higher on Sunday night.

The week ahead is crowded. Nvidia reports fiscal third-quarter results after the US close on Tuesday, with analysts looking for revenue growth near 100%. Anthropic is due to price its Nasdaq listing, marketed at $70 to $78 a share, on Wednesday and start trading on Thursday. In Asia, Japan's economy unexpectedly shrank in the third quarter, and India publishes October wholesale inflation at noon today, after retail inflation crossed the RBI's 6% ceiling.

top: Altimeter and Atreides urge Nvidia's board to keep Jensen Huang's return on the table; a supporters' petition tops 160,000 signatures.
Japan's GDP shrank at an annualised 0.1% in the third quarter against forecasts of growth, dragging Tokyo shares lower on Monday.
Activist Sachem Head has built a roughly 9% stake in Rightmove and wants the UK property portal to consider a sale.
SEBI has cleared Razorpay's ₹5,000–6,000 crore IPO and MakeMyTrip's India arm's offer-for-sale, while Indian startup funding slumped 90% last week.
Australian grocer Coles is investigating a weekend cybersecurity incident but says it has found no sign that data was taken.

items.fig: Week: S&P, Dow, Nasdaq each up more than 2%
items.headline: Wall Street Books Best Week Since August Despite Friday's Tech Slide
items.body: Indices pulled back on Friday as Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom fell, but still held strong weekly gains. Sunday-night futures pointed modestly higher, led by the Nasdaq-100.

items.headline: Japan's Economy Unexpectedly Contracts
items.body: Weak exports and high living costs produced the first contraction in four quarters, and the Nikkei fell in Monday trade. Markets still lean toward a Bank of Japan rate rise in December.

items.headline: Strong Dollar and High Yields Squeeze Gold and Crypto
items.body: The dollar hit its highest level since April 2025 as traders price a near-certain December Fed hike. Gold posted its biggest weekly fall since March and bitcoin slipped below $70,000.

items.fig: India WPI due 12:00 IST · Sep WPI 11.39%
items.headline: India Awaits Wholesale Inflation After CPI Breaches Ceiling
items.body: Forecasters expect October wholesale inflation above 12%, after retail inflation rose to 6.09%. The Nifty closed Friday at 25,144 but still gained about half a percent on the week.

items.fig: ≈$650bn lost in a week · HSBC target $170
items.headline: Nvidia Suffers Record Weekly Value Loss
items.body: The stock fell about 13% last week, its steepest weekly drop since April 2025, as HSBC downgraded it to hold. Results on Tuesday will be the first without Huang as CEO.

items.headline: Apple Hits a Record as Chip Stocks Retreat
items.body: Investors rotated toward the iPhone maker on Friday, lifting its market value above $5.2 trillion while semiconductor names reversed earlier gains.

items.headline: Online Beauty Retailer Crashes on Guidance Cut
items.body: Australia's Adore Beauty hit a record low after slashing its earnings outlook and reporting an 8% revenue fall, while agribusiness Elders rallied on a sharp profit increase.

items.headline: Korean Stocks Lead Asia Lower
items.body: Seoul's benchmark was the region's weakest market by midday Monday as chip-heavy indices stayed under pressure ahead of Nvidia's report.

items.headline: IDP Education Rebuffs Blackstone Again
items.body: The Australian student-placement company rejected a third takeover approach from the private equity firm.

items.headline: Tabcorp Moves for BetMakers
items.body: The wagering group has proposed buying the betting-technology provider, adding to a busy stretch of Australian dealmaking.

items.headline: Warburg Pincus Steps Back in Ingenia Contest
items.body: The buyout firm dropped its exclusivity with the land-lease operator, whose offer now trails a rival A$5.60-a-share proposal from AVID.

items.headline: InCred Buys Quintessentially's India Business
items.body: The financial services group acquired the Indian arm of the luxury concierge company; terms were not disclosed.

items.headline: Gerstner and Baker Press Nvidia's Board
items.body: The two growth-fund managers asked for a measured succession process that does not rule out Huang, acknowledging the board could still decide against it.

items.headline: Sachem Head Pushes Rightmove Toward a Sale
items.body: The New York activist has reportedly become the UK property portal's largest shareholder and wants it to engage with potential buyers. Rightmove rejected an approach from REA Group in 2024.

items.headline: Q3 13F Filings Land Today
items.body: Managers with more than $100 million in US equities must disclose their 30 September holdings, offering a view of positioning before the November AI sell-off.

items.headline: SEBI Clears Razorpay and MakeMyTrip India IPOs
items.body: Razorpay's listing could come in early 2027, and MakeMyTrip's Indian unit received approval for an offer-for-sale that could raise more than $1 billion.

items.headline: Indian Startup Funding Dries Up
items.body: Clean tech led a thin week in which Greenjoules was the largest round at $16 million. Consumer deals were small, including cloud-kitchen Hundo Pizza and fashion label QB Men.

items.headline: PlatinumRx in Talks for New Round
items.body: The online pharmacy is reportedly negotiating a raise at a valuation of $150 million to $200 million.

items.headline: Coles Probes Weekend Cyber Incident
items.body: The Australian supermarket chain says stores and online shopping are running normally and it has found no evidence of customer, staff or supplier data being taken.
